_comment: PLACE-NAME FINDINGS SOMEBODY HAS ALREADY LOOKED AT. Each entry is a review of one row, not a decision about a term: that is why it lives beside label-widths.json rather than inside overrides.json, and why the two share a folder without sharing a purpose. Read by the validator, in PlaceNameDrift. BEING IN THIS FILE IS BEING REVIEWED, so there is no `reviewed` field: a row nobody has looked at is simply absent, and there are thousands of those. What decides whether the finding is shown again is `review_action`. FOUR THINGS REOPEN A REVIEW AND ALL FOUR ARE MECHANICAL: the English moved (the row's corpus hash no longer matches `en`), the Spanish moved (the target's fingerprint no longer matches `es`), the rule moved (`expected` is no longer what the rule asks for that name), or the finding died (the name no longer appears in that row, and the entry is deleted -- the validator names them). A review is an opinion about one pairing of English, Spanish and rule; change any of the three and the opinion is about something that no longer exists. TRANSLATORS DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE: they deliver their reviews into agents-sharedarea alongside the translation and the coordinator merges them by gameKey + name, exactly as rows are promoted. The note on an entry may be written in Spanish; these comments may not.
_finding_comment: The only two findings there are, because the rule is binary and so is the state of the row: KO@MUST_BE_ENGLISH_BUT_ITS_TRANSLATED and KO@MUST_BE_TRANSLATED_BUT_FOUND_IN_ENGLISH. The two correct states (OK@...) never appear here: nobody reviews a row that is right.
_review_action_comment: SILENCES THE FINDING: `no_action@was_ok` (the translation was already right as it stands), `no_action@false_positive` (the finding was wrong, there is no toponym there) and `fixed` (the translation was changed). DOES NOT SILENCE IT: `not_fixed@out_of_slice` (a real defect, but the row belongs to another batch) and `not_fixed@needs_decision` (a real defect, but the Spanish is not settled). Those last two count as reviewed, so nobody triages them twice, and they still count as defects. THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN was_ok AND false_positive MATTERS: the first says the check was right and so was the translation; the second says the check was wrong, and once one name collects four of them the validator says so, because what needs fixing then is the check and not the rows.
_fields_comment: `gameKey` and `name` identify the finding. `finding`, `review_action` and `expected` (english | translated) are closed enumerations and the validator stops on any other value, naming the file and the entry. `en` and `es` are handed over by --toponym-report and must be copied from it rather than recomputed: `es` fingerprints the Spanish AS THE VALIDATOR SEES IT, and a leading (-Speaker-) label is stripped before the checks run. `reviewer` is ai@<agent> or human@<name>. `review_date` is ISO 8601 with a time. `note` is free text that only a person reads.
